name: Runtime (withruntime.com)
disclosure: Disclosure: battleships.dev, cited in this document, is built by the Boat team; Boat is one of the providers compared here. It is used as a cross-check, never as the sole source of a rate or verdict.

regions.value: One region: Virginia, United States. No region choice.
regions.quote: Everything runs in one region, in Virginia, United States

plans.name: Free usage (no credit)
plans.includedUsage: 100 GiB-hours of memory, 25 vCPU-hours of active CPU, 10 GB of saved copies and 5 GB of volumes; no card.

limits.maxSessionLength: No time limit unless timeoutSeconds is set (60 to 86,400 s).

plans.quote: Up to four sandboxes running at the same time, each up to 2 vCPU and 4 GiB of memory, with up to 10 GiB of disk

plans.name: Paid (prepaid credit, no plan)
plans.includedUsage: None beyond the monthly free usage. Prepay $10 to $10,000 by card; no plan fee, seat price or commitment.

limits.maxSessionLength: No time limit unless timeoutSeconds is set; a busy sandbox runs until stopped, idle-paused, or out of credit.

plans.quote: A paid account runs 100 sandboxes at once. ... One paid sandbox can have up to 16 vCPUs and 64 GiB of memory, at the same per-unit rates, and a disk of up to 400 GiB

plans.name: Paid with auto top-up
plans.includedUsage: Same rates and free usage; each automatic top-up adds 5% extra credit.

limits.maxSessionLength: No time limit unless timeoutSeconds is set.

plans.quote: While auto top-up is on with a saved card, the account runs 200 sandboxes at once instead of 100, with twice the vCPUs, memory and disk across them.

plans.name: Plans (private beta)
plans.includedUsage: A monthly fee returned as plan usage at the same measured prices; unused plan usage expires monthly. No prices published.
plans.quote: Plans are in a private beta. Only the organizations in it can see or choose one. ... A plan is a monthly fee that comes back as usage

rates.basis: measured CPU use, above a per-sandbox floor

original.unit: USD per vCPU-hour, billed as if always busy

rates.basis: allocated; every reserved vCPU billed as if fully busy
rates.quote: Reserved CPU keeps every vCPU for the sandbox and bills it as if it were always busy.

rates.basis: reserved memory, billed while compute runs

cpuBasisNote.value: CPU is billed on measured use, not on the vCPUs allocated. Reserved CPU is the opt-in exception and bills every vCPU as if always busy.
cpuBasisNote.quote: You pay for the CPU your code uses, not the CPUs it holds: $0.025 per active vCPU-hour and $0.0075 per reserved GiB-hour of memory.

floor.value: 50 millicores (0.05 vCPU) per sandbox by default; configurable with cpuFloorMillis, up to vcpu x 1000.
floor.quote: Waiting means memory plus the default CPU floor of 50 millicores, a twentieth of a vCPU.

billingIncrement.quote: Sandboxes you run bill as usual, per second.

minimum.value: No minimum billed time; no one-minute minimum.

perPlanDifferences.value: No plan or class changes the unit rates. Free, paid and plan accounts use the same $0.025/vCPU-hour and $0.0075/GiB-hour; a plan fee is returned as plan usage at those same prices. Reserved CPU is the only class change: it bills every vCPU as if always busy at the same rate.
perPlanDifferences.quote: Each month, the fee is given back as plan usage, at the same measured prices as any credit.

compute.notes: Memory is billed for the whole time compute runs, including while the code waits. CPU is billed from the moment the sandbox is ready. A running sandbox pauses itself after 300 seconds idle by default; idlePauseSeconds can be set from 60 to 86,400, or 0 to keep it running.

memoryBasis.value: Memory is billed for as long as compute runs, including while the code waits.
memoryBasis.quote: Memory is billed while compute runs.

idle.value: A sandbox pauses itself after 300 seconds with nothing happening; idlePauseSeconds can be set from 60 to 86,400, or 0 to keep it running.
idle.quote: A sandbox pauses itself after 300 seconds with nothing happening in it

sessionLimit.value: No maximum session length by default; timeoutSeconds can set a 60-to-86,400-second limit.
sessionLimit.quote: A sandbox has no time limit unless you set one with `timeoutSeconds`.

original.unit: USD per decimal GB (10^9 bytes) per 30-day month

disk.included: First 10 GiB of a running sandbox's disk is included; past that, only the blocks the disk alone holds are billed at the same rate.
disk.quote: The first 10 GiB of a running sandbox's disk is included. Past that, the blocks that only its disk holds are billed at the ... rate, $0.08 per decimal GB per 30-day month, measured every 30 seconds while it runs.

billedWhenStopped.value: Yes. Paused and stopped sandboxes are billed for disk and memory-snapshot blocks they alone own; paused CPU and RAM are not billed.
billedWhenStopped.quote: A paused sandbox keeps its files and memory for $0.08 per decimal GB per 30-day month.

original.unit: USD per decimal GB per 30-day month

snapshot.quote: $0.08 per decimal GB per 30-day month ... 119 microdollars per GiB-hour

volume.chargedOn: The full size you create it with, written or not.
volume.quote: 153 microdollars per GiB-hour ... about $0.11 per GiB per 30-day month

original.unit: USD per decimal GB per 30-day month

volumeBackup.quote: Volume backups cost $0.02 per decimal GB per 30-day month.

retention.value: A stopped or paused sandbox's disk is kept 30 days in an account that has bought credit or saved a card; any other item, and every item in an account that has done neither, is kept 7 days. Snapshots are kept as long as the account has credit, 7 days without.
retention.quote: A stopped or paused sandbox's disk is kept for 30 days in an account that has bought credit or saved a card. Any other item, and every item in an account that has done neither, is kept for seven days.

snapshotRetention.value: A snapshot is kept as long as the account has credit, 7 days without credit, unless a 1-to-365-day retention is set.
snapshotRetention.quote: A snapshot is kept as long as you have credit, with no end date (7 days without credit), unless you choose 1 to 365 days.

billingIncrement.value: Storage is paid an hour at a time from the balance.
billingIncrement.quote: Storage is paid an hour at a time from your balance.

egress.included: First 100 GiB per account per month free.

original.unit: USD per decimal GB past 100 GiB/month

egress.quote: Each account's first 100 GiB of outbound traffic a month is free. After that, it costs $0.02 per decimal GB.

other.name: Dedicated IPv4
other.quote: A dedicated IPv4 address costs $5 per 30-day month.

other.name: WireGuard tunnel (up to 16 peers)
other.quote: A WireGuard tunnel costs $5 per 30-day month, including up to 16 peers.

other.name: Seats, plan fee, minimum spend
other.quote: There is no plan fee, no seat price and no commitment.

other.name: Booked burst capacity not used
other.price: $0.001875 per GiB-hour (a quarter of the memory rate)
other.quote: Booked room that none of them uses costs a quarter of the memory rate, $0.001875 per GiB-hour, with no CPU charge.

freeTier.what: 100 free hours of a 1 GB machine: 100 GiB-hours of memory and 25 vCPU-hours of active CPU, plus 10 GB of saved copies and 5 GB of volumes.
freeTier.conditions: Once across the first 30 days for an account that has never paid; every month, renewed on the 1st (UTC), once the account has paid. No card.
freeTier.limits: 4 sandboxes at once, 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB disk each, 8 vCPU / 16 GiB across running sandboxes, 5 sandboxes kept, 50 created per 24 hours.
freeTier.quote: Every account gets free usage, with no card, after a verified sign-in. It is 100 free hours of a 1 GB machine.
freeTier.limitsQuote: At most 8 vCPU and 16 GiB at the same time across every sandbox and image build that is running. ... At most 50 sandboxes made a day

networkCaveat.value: An account opened from a data-centre or VPN network gets its free usage only after it adds credit.
networkCaveat.quote: An account opened from a data-centre or VPN network (a cloud provider's address, or a VPN company's) gets its free usage once it adds credit, not before.

diffs.quote: At most 5 sandboxes kept, running, paused or stopped.

diffs.battleships: 0 (active_floor field; its note says the 0.05-vCPU floor cannot be encoded)
diffs.quote: Waiting means memory plus the default CPU floor of 50 millicores, a twentieth of a vCPU.

lifecycle.title: Time and lifetime: pause, stop or delete

deploy.oneClickOrManaged: Not found. No Hermes Agent or OpenClaw guide, template or managed option exists in Runtime's docs index; /docs/hermes.md and /docs/openclaw.md return HTTP 404 "Guide not found".
deploy.officialTemplateOrGuide: Not found for Hermes Agent or OpenClaw.
deploy.manualRoute: Sign in, press Start a sandbox on Home for a browser shell, then install Hermes with its install script inside the sandbox, set a model provider key, and keep the sandbox with persistent: true so it does not idle-pause. Runtime documents the sandbox and persistence; it does not document Hermes.
deploy.nonCoderDashboardOnly: Partly. The dashboard creates a sandbox and opens a shell in the page, and a Desktop product exists, but installing and configuring Hermes still means typing shell commands and editing a model config. No click-only route is documented.

urls.quote: It opens with a shell running in the page, on your free hours.
persistent: true keeps a sandbox running until you stop it, with no idle pause.
